```{r}
evaluation <- readr::read_csv(here::here("outputs", "audits", "selected-evaluation.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cohort <- readr::read_csv(here::here("outputs", "tables", "cohort-flow.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

if (nrow(evaluation) != 1L) stop("Expected exactly one selected FIA evaluation record.")
evaluation_id <- format(evaluation$evalid[[1]], scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

effect_row <- function(effect_label, required = FALSE) {
  result <- odds |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$label == .env$effect_label) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)
  if (required && nrow(result) != 1L) stop("Required model effect not found: ", effect_label)
  result
}
format_effect <- function(effect) {
  sprintf(
    "OR %.2f, 95%% CI %.2f–%.2f",
    effect$estimate[[1]], effect$conf.low[[1]], effect$conf.high[[1]]
  )
}

coverage_effect <- effect_row("Microplot condition coverage", required = TRUE)
temperature_effect <- effect_row("Mean annual temperature")
precipitation_effect <- effect_row("Annual precipitation")
age_effect <- effect_row("Stand age")
disturbance_effect <- effect_row("Recorded disturbance")

curve_value <- function(x, field = "predicted_probability") {
  stats::approx(effect_curve$maple_ba_ft2_ac, effect_curve[[field]], xout = x, rule = 2)$y
}
curve_zero <- curve_value(0)
curve_moderate_ba <- 25
curve_moderate <- curve_value(curve_moderate_ba)
spline_comparison <- functional_form |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Natural spline", .data$model)) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)
plot_random_candidate <- random_structure |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$model == "County plus plot visit") |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)
cv_metric <- function(metric_name) {
  value <- validation$value[validation$metric == metric_name]
  if (length(value) != 1L) stop("Required validation metric not found: ", metric_name)
  value
}
dharma_p <- function(test_name) {
  value <- dharma_tests$p_value[dharma_tests$diagnostic == test_name]
  if (length(value) != 1L) stop("Required DHARMa test not found: ", test_name)
  value
}
precipitation_sensitivity <- inference_sensitivity |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$label == "Annual precipitation") |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)

climate_statements <- character()
if (nrow(temperature_effect)) {
  climate_statements <- c(
    climate_statements,
    paste0("The temperature proxy had ", format_effect(temperature_effect), ".")
  )
}
if (nrow(precipitation_effect)) {
  climate_statements <- c(
    climate_statements,
    paste0(
      "The precipitation proxy had ", format_effect(precipitation_effect),
      ", but its Wald p-value was ", sprintf("%.3f", precipitation_effect$p.value),
      ", BH-adjusted p-value was ", sprintf("%.3f", precipitation_sensitivity$mixed_model_bh_p_value),
      ", and the county-cluster sensitivity p-value was ", sprintf("%.3f", precipitation_sensitivity$cluster_robust_p_value),
      "; it is therefore treated as weak and exploratory."
    )
  )
}
climate_text <- if (length(climate_statements)) {
  paste(
    "The retained county-scale climate terms described a broad geographic gradient.",
    paste(climate_statements, collapse = " "),
    "These coefficients must not be read as plot-level climate effects."
  )
} else {
  "County-scale climate terms were not retained by the pre-specified support and correlation checks."
}

other_effects <- dplyr::bind_rows(age_effect, disturbance_effect)
null_other_effects <- other_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$conf.low <= 1, .data$conf.high >= 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$label)
other_effects_text <- if (!nrow(other_effects)) {
  "Stand age and recorded disturbance were not retained by the data-support checks."
} else if (length(null_other_effects)) {
  paste0(
    "The 95% confidence intervals crossed one for ",
    paste(tolower(null_other_effects), collapse = " and "), "."
  )
} else {
  "The retained stand age or disturbance intervals did not cross one."
}

fixed_effect_text <- paste(c("nonlinear sugar-maple basal area", odds$label), collapse = ", ")
cohort_n <- function(step_name) {
  value <- cohort$observations[cohort$step == step_name]
  if (length(value) != 1L) stop("Cohort step not found: ", step_name)
  scales::comma(value)
}
```

## Abstract {.unnumbered}

This exploratory study evaluated `r scales::comma(summary$plot_conditions)` plot-condition measurements from FIA's maple/beech/birch forest-type group, used here as the operational northern-hardwood cohort, across `r summary$counties` Michigan counties. It asked whether places with substantial established sugar maple also showed evidence of the next cohort. Sugar-maple seedlings were tallied in `r scales::percent(summary$maple_seedling_detected / summary$seedling_sampled, accuracy = 0.1)` of conditions with demonstrated microplot sampling opportunity. A transparent, sample-relative indicator flagged `r scales::comma(summary$potential_gaps)` observations (`r scales::percent(summary$potential_gap_fraction, accuracy = 0.1)`) combining upper-third sugar-maple basal-area share with no sugar-maple seedlings tallied. Associations were evaluated with `r support$model_type`, and geographic generalization was checked by holding out whole counties. Results describe the analyzed sample and do not constitute FIA design-based population estimates or causal effects.

## Why regeneration matters

Northern hardwood forests can retain a mature sugar-maple canopy even when younger cohorts are sparse. That mismatch is relevant to future composition, but it does not by itself identify a mechanism. Browsing, competition, site conditions, management history, disturbance, seed availability, and sampling variability can all contribute.

This project therefore asks a deliberately bounded question:

> Among contemporary Michigan FIA northern-hardwood observations, which stand and broad-scale climate characteristics are associated with whether sugar-maple seedlings were tallied?

## Data

:::: {.columns .source-grid .column-page}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Forest Inventory and Analysis

The analysis uses the Michigan SQLite release from the U.S. Forest Service FIA DataMart [@usfs_datamart]. FIA reference tables, rather than undocumented numeric constants, identify sugar maple and the retained forest types. The analytical key is a plot visit and condition (`PLT_CN + CONDID`). TREE and SEEDLING records are aggregated independently before they are joined, preventing a tree-by-seedling Cartesian product.

Exact FIA plot locations are confidential. Public FIA coordinates may be approximate; this analysis neither uses nor infers them. County identifiers supplied by FIA provide the only spatial link used here.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Climate

Daymet Version 4 R1 provides daily 1-km temperature and precipitation estimates [@thornton2022daymet]. For each Michigan county, this analysis uses the Daymet cell at an interior representative location to construct a 1991–2020 climate normal. These values are broad county proxies, not plot-level measurements.
:::
::::

Release v1.2.0 pins the Michigan `EXPCURR` evaluation “`r evaluation$eval_descr`” (EVALID `r evaluation_id`; inventory window `r evaluation$start_invyr`–`r evaluation$end_invyr`). It then filters assigned visits to sampled, accessible conditions in FIA's maple/beech/birch forest-type group, the project's operational northern-hardwood cohort. The assigned measurement records span `r summary$years_min`–`r summary$years_max`. Conditions without demonstrated microplot sampling opportunity do not receive an inferred seedling zero.

## Methods

::::: {.method-grid .column-page}
:::: {.method-card}
[01 · Resolve]{.method-label}

**Reference-driven cohort**

Species and forest types resolve from FIADB reference tables rather than hidden constants; the published release pins its documented evaluation identifier.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[02 · Aggregate]{.method-label}

**Condition-level ecology**

TREE and SEEDLING records aggregate independently before joining at `PLT_CN + CONDID`.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[03 · Enrich]{.method-label}

**Protected spatial link**

County identifiers connect 1991–2020 Daymet proxies without using or inferring confidential plot locations.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[04 · Estimate]{.method-label}

**Cluster-aware inference**

The supported logistic model carries a county random intercept, a nonlinear maple response, and transparent support and validation checks.
::::
:::::

### Established sugar maple

For every live TREE record, basal-area contribution on the FIA plot basis is calculated as

$$
BA_i = 0.005454 \times DIA_i^2 \times TPA_{i,unadj},
$$

where diameter is in inches and the resulting contribution is in square feet per acre on the unadjusted sample basis. Expansion to condition density occurs **record by record** using the proportion for the tree's sampling frame: `MICRPROP_UNADJ` for trees below 5 inches diameter, `SUBPPROP_UNADJ` for larger subplot trees, and `MACRPROP_UNADJ` only when a populated macroplot breakpoint applies. Equivalently,

$$
BA_c = \sum_{i \in c}\frac{0.005454 \times DIA_i^2 \times TPA_{i,unadj}}
{PROP_{c,frame(i),unadj}}.
$$

Sugar-maple basal-area share divides the resulting frame-corrected sugar-maple density by frame-corrected total live-tree density within the condition.

As a strict calculation check, derived live-tree basal area agreed with FIA's condition-level `BALIVE` field across `r scales::comma(ba_check$observations)` conditions (Pearson *r* = `r sprintf("%.6f", ba_check$pearson_correlation)`; mean absolute error `r sprintf("%.6f", ba_check$mean_absolute_error_ft2_ac)` ft²/acre; maximum absolute error `r sprintf("%.6f", ba_check$max_absolute_error_ft2_ac)` ft²/acre).

### Regeneration

SEEDLING `TPA_UNADJ` values are aggregated by species and plot-condition. The primary response is binary detection. A zero means no sugar-maple seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots; it is not proof that the entire condition lacked seedlings.

### Exploratory regeneration-gap indicator

The hero figure flags a **potential regeneration gap** when a condition has:

1. sugar-maple basal-area share in the upper third among conditions with demonstrated seedling sampling; and
2. no sugar-maple seedlings tallied.

The continuous companion indicator is the percentile rank of established share minus the percentile rank of log seedling density. Neither measure is presented as a validated ecological index.

### Model

The supported model is a `r support$model_type` with no-sugar-maple-seedlings-tallied as the response. Sugar-maple basal area enters as a 3-df natural spline of standardized `log1p` basal area; the spline improved AIC by `r sprintf("%.1f", functional_form$aic[[1]] - spline_comparison$aic)` and the nested likelihood-ratio test gave *p* = `r format.pval(spline_comparison$likelihood_ratio_p_value, digits = 2)`. Other continuous predictors are standardized within the final model-complete cohort, and their conventional coefficient summaries use model-based Wald 95% intervals. Retained fixed effects were `r fixed_effect_text`.

The fitted random-effects structure is a county random intercept. Adding a plot-visit intercept produced a small variance (`r sprintf("%.4f", plot_random_candidate$plot_visit_variance)`), no support in a boundary-aware variance-component comparison (*p* = `r sprintf("%.3f", plot_random_candidate$boundary_mixture_p_value)`), and an AIC `r sprintf("%.1f", plot_random_candidate$aic - random_structure$aic[random_structure$selected])` points higher, so the parsimonious county-only structure was retained. The model uses `r scales::comma(support$model_complete_n)` complete conditions (`r scales::percent(support$model_complete_fraction_of_cohort, accuracy = 0.1)` of the `r scales::comma(support$analytical_cohort_n)`-condition analytical cohort) from `r scales::comma(support$plot_visits)` plot visits across `r support$counties` counties. There were `r round(support$events_per_parameter, 1)` outcome events per non-intercept fixed-effect coefficient.

::: {.table-panel .column-page}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-specification
#| tbl-cap: "Release model specification and support."
model_specification <- tibble::tibble(
  Item = c(

    "Counties", "Plot visits", "Multi-condition plot visits", "Events per fixed coefficient"
  ),
  Value = c(
    support$model_formula,
    scales::comma(support$events_no_seedlings),
    scales::comma(support$events_seedlings),
    paste0(
      scales::comma(support$model_complete_n), " / ", scales::comma(support$analytical_cohort_n),
      " (", scales::percent(support$model_complete_fraction_of_cohort, accuracy = 0.1), ")"
    ),
    scales::comma(support$counties),
    scales::comma(support$plot_visits),
    scales::comma(support$multi_condition_plot_visits),
    sprintf("%.1f", support$events_per_parameter)
  )
)
knitr::kable(model_specification, align = c("l", "l"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-effects

effect_table <- odds |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Predictor = .data$label,
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", .data$estimate),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", .data$conf.low, .data$conf.high),
    `p-value` = dplyr::if_else(.data$p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", .data$p.value))
  )

```

::: {.result-interpretation .column-page}
[Reading the model]{.result-interpretation-label}

The established-maple association was nonlinear. At the report's reference profile (other continuous predictors at their model-cohort means, no recorded disturbance, and the county random effect set to zero), the adjusted probability of no seedlings tallied declined from `r scales::percent(curve_zero, accuracy = 1)` at zero maple basal area to `r scales::percent(curve_moderate, accuracy = 1)` at `r curve_moderate_ba` ft²/acre, then leveled off. These are conditional profile contrasts from an observational model, not causal probabilities for every forest condition. Greater microplot condition coverage was also associated with lower non-detection odds (OR `r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$estimate)`, Wald 95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$conf.high)`), reinforcing why sampling opportunity belongs in the model.

`r climate_text` `r other_effects_text`
:::

### Model adequacy

::::: {.model-audit-grid .column-page}
:::: {.model-audit-card}
[**Converged**]{.model-audit-value}

optimizer criterion
::::

:::: {.model-audit-card}
[**Non-singular**]{.model-audit-value}

random-effects structure
::::

:::: {.model-audit-card}
[**`r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("Brier score"))`**]{.model-audit-value}

county-held-out Brier score
::::

:::: {.model-audit-card}
[**`r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("ROC AUC"))`**]{.model-audit-value}

county-held-out ROC AUC
::::
:::::

Ten-fold cross-validation assigned entire counties rather than individual records to folds. Scaling and spline transformations were learned again inside each training fold, and held-out counties were predicted from fixed effects only. Across all `r scales::comma(support$model_complete_n)` assessment predictions, Brier score was `r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("Brier score"))`, ROC AUC was `r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("ROC AUC"))`, calibration intercept was `r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("Calibration intercept"))`, and calibration slope was `r sprintf("%.3f", cv_metric("Calibration slope"))`. For comparison, the conditional in-sample Brier score was `r sprintf("%.3f", support$in_sample_brier_conditional)`; it is not presented as out-of-county performance.

```{r}
#| label: fig-model-diagnostics
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "Simulation-based DHARMa diagnostics for the supported mixed-effects logistic model: uniform-quantile agreement and scaled residuals versus fitted conditional probability."
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel model diagnostic. Ordered scaled residuals closely follow the expected uniform line. Residuals versus fitted probabilities are broadly centered around one half, with a slight low-probability pattern."
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("outputs", "figures", "model_diagnostics.png"))
```

No simulation-based check crossed the pre-specified 0.05 flag: uniformity *p* = `r sprintf("%.3f", dharma_p("uniformity"))`, dispersion *p* = `r sprintf("%.3f", dharma_p("dispersion"))`, and outlier *p* = `r sprintf("%.3f", dharma_p("outliers"))`. The combined residual-quantile check was borderline (*p* = `r sprintf("%.3f", dharma_p("residual_quantiles"))`), so absence of a formal flag is not treated as proof of perfect model fit.

Gray counties are deliberately suppressed rather than assigned unstable fractions. The interval panel shows unweighted binomial reference uncertainty only; it ignores the FIA survey design and within-county clustering.

## Discussion

:::: {.interpretation-grid .column-page}
::: {.interpretation-card .interpretation-supported}
[What the evidence supports]{.interpretation-kicker}

- A transparent screen for canopy–cohort mismatch in the analyzed sample.
- Adjusted associations with seedling non-detection under the supported model.
- Reproducible hypotheses for field or design-based follow-up.
:::

::: {.interpretation-card .interpretation-boundary}
[What it does not establish]{.interpretation-kicker}

- Statewide prevalence or formal FIA population estimates.
- A causal effect of canopy, climate, browsing, or disturbance.
- Exact plot-level climate exposure or long-term cohort survival.
:::
::::

The analysis makes the distinction between established live-tree basal area and observed seedling recruitment visible. Under the primary rule, `r summary$potential_gaps` of `r summary$seedling_sampled` sampled conditions were flagged. Raising the established-maple threshold from an upper-third share of `r scales::percent(thresholds$primary_established_threshold, accuracy = 0.1)` to an upper-quartile share of `r scales::percent(thresholds$sensitivity_established_threshold, accuracy = 0.1)` reduced the flag count to `r thresholds$sensitivity_gap_n` (`r scales::percent(thresholds$sensitivity_gap_fraction, accuracy = 0.1)`). This sensitivity is a reason to treat the flag as a screening device rather than a fixed ecological category.

The model estimates which measured stand and broad climate attributes covary with seedling detection after adjustment for the other retained terms. The maple curve and pointwise Wald intervals are the primary association evidence; county-grouped validation separately assesses discrimination and calibration outside the fitted counties.

The results should be interpreted as hypotheses and patterns worthy of follow-up. A seedling tally is an imperfect window into recruitment, and seedlings do not guarantee survival into sapling or canopy cohorts.

## Limitations

1. **Confidential locations.** Exact FIA plot locations are confidential. Public coordinates may be approximate; the analysis neither uses nor infers them, relying on county IDs alone.
2. **Sampling opportunity.** A zero means no seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots, not ecological absence across the condition.
3. **Observational design.** Associations are not causal effects.
4. **Sample versus population.** `TPA_UNADJ` and frame proportions expand records within the plot design; they are not statewide survey weights. Formal statewide estimates require FIA evaluation, stratum, adjustment, and sampling-error procedures [@bechtold2005sampling].
5. **Exploratory indicator.** The gap flag is sample-relative and threshold-dependent.
6. **County summaries.** Wilson intervals are unweighted descriptive references that ignore survey design and within-county clustering.
7. **Unmeasured drivers.** Deer browsing, soils, management history, competition, and other factors are incompletely represented.
8. **Temporal alignment.** Climate normals summarize 1991–2020 and do not reproduce weather immediately preceding each measurement.

:::: {.repro-card}

Raw data are excluded from version control. Source URLs, cached-file retrieval timestamps, file sizes, and checksums for each county's Daymet API response are recorded in `outputs/audits/data-provenance.csv`. Important joins record row counts, unique keys, and unmatched keys. The public repository includes a curated [release validation record](https://github.com/dineshpotla/canopy-to-cohort/blob/main/outputs/audits/release-validation.csv) and [aggregate model-support evidence](https://github.com/dineshpotla/canopy-to-cohort/blob/main/outputs/tables/model-support.csv).

GitHub Actions runs the data-free unit-test subset; tests requiring derived FIA data or a fitted model skip cleanly on a fresh clone. The completed v1.2.0 local build and its exact expectation counts are recorded in the release-validation artifact. From a fresh clone, the full analysis runs with:

```bash
make setup
make acquire
make all
```

Package versions are recorded in `renv.lock`. The release was tested with R 4.6.1 and Quarto 1.9.38. FIA's state archive URL is mutable, so acquisition compares downloaded source sizes and SHA-256 hashes with the v1.0.0–v1.2.0 manifest and warns when a current-data rerun is not byte-identical to the published source snapshot.
